C1.rationale: Constraint density is low and the few hard directives concern real contracts or irreversible steps and state their reason; residual style prescriptions in the Conventions section ('use tables', 'include both short and long flag forms') are phrased as prohibitions rather than delegated judgment, which keeps it from 4.

C2.rationale: A memory file with no invocable interface: no arguments, flags, or parameter surface to make self-describing.

C3.rationale: Detail is deferred aggressively and by name: a 38-row index of separately-loadable rule files plus explicit 'see X' pointers to skill-development.md, agentic-optimization.md, docs/pi-export.md, adapters/README.md and docs/blueprint/README.md; short of 5 because rare reference detail (marketplace entry JSON, release-please-config block, manifest snippet) is still inlined in the entry point rather than split out.

evidence.quote: | `.claude/rules/hooks-reference.md` | Complete hook event reference (2.1.50+): all events, schemas, timeouts, PermissionRequest |

C4.rationale: Several sections restate guidance that already lives in an auto-injected rule file and then point at that same file: the Agentic Optimization bullets duplicate agentic-optimization.md's compact-output/fail-fast/CI-mode principles, and the Git Workflow section reproduces the format, type list and worked example from conventional-commits.md before deferring to it; the naming bullets overlap skill-naming.md. The excellent rules index shows the file knows the pointer-only pattern, which is why the copies stand out.

C5.rationale: Most of the file fails the every-turn test: an ASCII tree of a layout visible from the repo, a Plugin Organization table, and four multi-step procedures (skill creation, user-invocable skill creation, plugin lifecycle create/delete with inline JSON, development workflow) that only matter once a user asks for that specific task and are exactly the material the rubric says to promote to a skill and reference by name. Real gotchas are present (blueprint disabled-task reasons, autonomy-level-3 consumer-only, the pi tier-vs-adapter successor state, the deliberately non-matching blueprint commit scope) but occupy a minority of the tokens; two orphaned rule rows appended after the Conventions bullet list show the surface is large enough to drift.

evidence.quote: When creating, modifying, or deleting a plugin, update these files:

C6.rationale: Where work is mechanical the file names the artifact that owns it rather than describing the check in prose: a YAML classification file as source of truth with its enforcing script, CI drift checks by script path, and just recipes as the runnable entry points; short of 5 because it rarely says whether to run or read the artifact, and the plugin-creation config is spelled out as literal snippets where a scaffolding script or schema could state it.

evidence.quote: The `Plugin: Enablement drift` check (`scripts/check-enabled-plugins-drift.sh`) fails CI if a marketplace plugin is left disabled.

top_finding: Promote the four always-loaded procedures (Creating New Skills, Creating User-Invocable Skills, Plugin Lifecycle, Development Workflow) into an authoring skill and leave one named reference line each, so the always-loaded surface keeps only the gotchas.
counter_finding: The Blueprint constrained-dogfooding section earns its tokens outright: the disabled-task reasons, the consumer-only autonomy-level-3 caveat and the deliberately non-matching `blueprint` commit scope are non-discoverable traps that would cause real damage if a model re-derived them from the repo.

an ASCII tree of a layout any reader sees from the filesystem
a valuable named index, but several row descriptions have grown into paragraph summaries and two rows have drifted outside the table
a scaffolding procedure that only matters once a skill is actually being authored
same task-triggered frontmatter procedure, split across two sections
restates agentic-optimization.md and then points at it
taxonomy inferable from the plugin directory names
long create/delete checklist with inline JSON, needed only when a plugin is added or removed
the automation contract is worth one line; the format spec, type list and worked example belong solely to conventional-commits.md
a generic seven-step process the model would follow anyway
the tier-vs-adapter successor state is a genuine gotcha; the recipe inventory belongs in the linked docs
non-discoverable constraints whose violation causes real damage
naming rules overlap skill-naming.md and the table/flag bullets are style prescriptions

house_standards_seen: CLAUDE.md itself is auto-injected into every agent context in this repo, so the unit under judgment was already present before I read it

several .claude/rules/*.md are auto-injected too (pr-branch-sync, loop-integrity, bash-tool-replacements, gh-json-fields, parallel-safe-queries, terminology, conventional-commits, task-id-stability, offload-to-deterministic-substrate, docs-currency, agent-coworker-detection, handling-blocked-hooks)
the excluded house conventions (conventional-commit scopes, release-please dogfooding, plugin lifecycle bookkeeping) are visible in the injected copy
leakage.note: I re-read CLAUDE.md from disk and scored that file; all quotes were taken from the on-disk read. The injected rule files were used only as C4 evidence that specific guidance already has another owner (agentic-optimization.md, conventional-commits.md, skill-naming.md), which the rubric explicitly permits judges to discover. I did not score the desirability of any excluded house convention: the Git Workflow and Plugin Lifecycle sections were assessed only for single-sourcing and always-loaded cost, never for whether the conventions themselves are correct. I did not open any of the prohibited files.
